label: Local Reaper piece at a station of a descent of moments
definition: PieceAt R u c n holds when, in world u, the station at moment c n of the sequence c obeys four rules: (1) positive trigger: if the output register of the station at c (n + 1), the next earlier moment of the sequence, is empty, the station at c n issues; (2) emission: if it issues, its output carries its own code c n; (3) forwarding: any code on the earlier station's output is copied unchanged to its own; (4) admissibility: any code on its output names a station of the same sequence at or before it (c j with n <= j). Rules 1-3 relate only the registers at c n and c (n + 1). Rule 4 constrains only the register at c n but refers to every upstream slot of the whole sequence, so a piece depends on the whole descent, not only on its neighbour. In ordinary language: one Grim Reaper or Placer station doing its job, whose output may carry only codes issued within the sequence.
note: Analyst definition; attribution deferred. The four rules are the moment-placed counterparts of IndexedSignalReaper's PositiveTrigger, Emission, Forwarding and IndexAdmissible (the indexed-signal definitions). Admissibility is the clause that excludes a code from a source outside the descent, for instance from a station at the accumulation point 0 of t, t/2, ... in [0, t]; that is exactly where [0, t] and the open-below (0, t] differ, so the Benardete parity in the Grim Reaper objection audit turns on it. The piece at n and the piece at n + 1 share the register at c (n + 1); co-possibility asks for both in one world. Witnesses for different adjacent pairs may put different contents on a shared register, and they cannot all agree (GrimReaperPatchwork overlapAgreeingWitnessesImpossible): a piece duplicates a station with its rules, not its register contents. Two adjacent pieces are jointly realized in one world for every descent of integer times (GrimReaperPatchwork control 2, pivot registers). Whether a real station can be built to these rules at given moments is OPEN.
